answers.children: Glen of Imaal Terriers are moderately good with children. Their affectionate nature makes them loyal with family but their tenacious terrier build and independent streak mean they have low tolerance for poking or pulling by toddlers, and their history of vermin control can surface as chasing small moving things.
answers.other-pets: Glen of Imaal Terriers do not always get along with other pets. Bred for vermin control and small game hunting they retain a strong prey drive that leads to chasing small animals, and their stubborn independence can create tension especially with same-sex dogs around the home.
answers.exercise: Glen of Imaal Terriers need around an hour of exercise daily. Split between brisk walks and backyard play this prevents boredom that otherwise turns into digging up gardens, while their short sturdy legs from badger-hunting ancestry mean they tire on long hikes and suit moderate activity instead.
answers.shedding: Yes — Glen of Imaal Terriers shed moderately. Their medium double coat with wiry texture traps loose hair around the home and requires regular attention to stop matting especially on the sturdy body shaped by generations of rugged Irish farm work.
answers.hypoallergenic: No breed is truly hypoallergenic and the Glen of Imaal Terrier is not one of those commonly suggested for allergy sufferers. Its medium double coat with wiry outer layer still releases dander and hair in keeping with its tough working heritage from County Wicklow.
answers.training: Glen of Imaal Terriers are not easy to train. Their independent temperament and history as silent vermin controllers in Ireland make them stubborn and slow to respond to commands, though their intelligence of 7 can help when training sessions stay short and focused on their tenacious drive.
answers.lifespan: Glen of Imaal Terriers live 10-15 years. Their health robustness of 7 and sturdy short-legged build developed for digging into burrows and badger hunting in harsh Irish hills support a typical lifespan for a small working terrier when their energetic needs are met through daily activity and mental outlets.
answers.size: Glen of Imaal Terriers reach 32-40 lb and stand 12-14 in at the shoulder. This compact muscular build with short sturdy legs from their turnspit and hunting past feels solid and low to the ground making them a substantial small dog that is easy to manage indoors yet powerful enough for determined work.
answers.barking: Glen of Imaal Terriers bark moderately. Bred to work silently while controlling vermin and hunting badgers in Ireland they reserve their deep serious voice for important alerts rather than constant yapping, though their tenacious personality can prompt barking at squirrels or intruders if instincts are not channelled.
answers.apartment: Glen of Imaal Terriers can live in an apartment. Their moderate energy of 6 and affectionate loyalty let them settle indoors provided they receive an hour of daily exercise and outlets for digging and chasing to prevent destructive behaviour from their independent terrier heritage.
answers.first-time: Glen of Imaal Terriers are not a good first dog. Their stubbornness and slow trainability combined with a strong prey drive for chasing and digging demand consistent management that can overwhelm novices despite the breed’s loyal affectionate side with family.
